rewrites.title: Single-cell lineage-resolved memory and mitotic bookmarking
rewrites.description: Combine live-cell FOS/JUN reporters or barcoded lineage tracing with single-cell multiome readouts, and image or profile AP-1 on mitotic chromatin. Test whether sister cells share memory states and AP-1 occupancy, and whether blocking division or bookmarking alters inheritance.

rewrites.title: Acute degron removal and restoration of AP-1 with single-molecule tracking
rewrites.description: Use an auxin/dTAG degron to fully remove AP-1 protein for a defined window during the maintenance phase, then restore it and test recall; simultaneously measure AP-1 residence times and turnover by live single-molecule tracking and SNAP-tag pulse-chase. If memory survives transient total loss of AP-1, the information is stored elsewhere and AP-1 is a reader or relay; if it does not, AP-1 occupancy is itself the store.

rewrites.title: Mitotic transmission: AP-1 bookmarking and post-division state recovery
rewrites.description: Combine live imaging of tagged JUN/FOS through mitosis with mitotic chromatin profiling (e.g., CUT&RUN on sorted mitotic cells) and sister-cell comparisons of expression after division. Concordance between sister cells beyond what noise predicts, plus retention of AP-1 at mitotic chromatin, would support heritable rather than merely slow-decaying memory.

rewrites.title: Post-replication single-molecule footprinting of AP-1 enhancers
rewrites.description: Combine nascent-strand labeling with single-molecule methyltransferase footprinting (Fiber-seq/SAMOSA) to ask whether AP-1 motifs on newly replicated daughter chromatin are re-opened and co-occupied in cis, and how fast. This tests whether the state is re-established on both daughter molecules after each round of replication, a requirement for epigenetic memory.

rewrites.title: Hysteresis loop mapping
rewrites.description: Titrate a stimulus (e.g., TNF, serum, or optogenetic c-Fos/c-Jun induction) up and then down. Measure single-cell AP-1 activity and target-gene expression to test whether the response at identical input depends on prior history, and quantify loop area and decay time after stimulus removal.

rewrites.title: Lineage-tracked test of heritable persistence
rewrites.description: Prime cells, then track single-cell lineages with live reporters of AP-1 activity and chromatin state through several divisions, comparing with mock-treated lineages. Persistence of the primed state across divisions without ongoing stimulation, measured against a null model of stochastic heterogeneity, would indicate a self-sustaining, heritable memory rather than transient signaling.

rewrites.title: Secondary challenge assays with single-cell multiome readout
rewrites.description: Prime cells, rest them, and then re-challenge with the same or a different stimulus. Use paired scRNA/scATAC-seq to quantify faster, stronger, or more sensitized induction of AP-1 target genes in primed versus naive cells, and relate this to prior accessibility at specific enhancers. Single-cell resolution distinguishes a graded shift in all cells from an all-or-none switch in a subpopulation.

rewrites.title: AP-1 occupancy and chromatin accessibility time course
rewrites.description: Run CUT&RUN/ATAC-seq/footprinting at high time resolution during and after priming to measure whether AP-1 motifs at latent enhancers stay accessible, H3K27ac-marked, and AP-1-bound after the factor's own levels return to baseline. Pair this with testing dependence on BAF/SWI-SNF to show whether memory resides in the chromatin state left by AP-1 or in continued AP-1 binding.

rewrites.title: Single-cell lineage-tracked reporter for an AP-1 enhancer
rewrites.description: Build a knock-in destabilized fluorescent reporter at an AP-1-responsive enhancer, pulse cells, sort by reporter state after rest, and track daughter cells by live imaging over several generations. This tests whether memory is bimodal rather than a population average and whether it is inherited across divisions.

rewrites.title: Live single-cell reporter tracking through divisions
rewrites.description: Knock a fluorescent reporter into an AP-1 target locus (e.g., FOSL1 or an enhancer-driven reporter) and track primed and naive cells by time-lapse microscopy across several generations after washout. Quantify whether the faster re-induction state is bimodal and whether it is inherited by daughter cells (sibling and lineage correlations), testing population averaging and mitotic heritability.

rewrites.title: Single-cell lineage-resolved memory with live AP-1 reporters
rewrites.description: Tag endogenous Fos/Jun and a target gene with fluorescent reporters, and track primed cells and their descendants by live imaging across divisions. Compare sister-cell correlations and decay kinetics with those of unprimed controls to quantify heritability and test whether memory is cell-autonomous and AP-1 dependent.

rewrites.title: Cross-stimulus test of memory specificity
rewrites.description: Prime cells with one AP-1-inducing stimulus, then challenge them with an unrelated stimulus that activates a non-AP-1 program, or with an AP-1 stimulus that activates a different gene set. Measure whether priming shifts the response to the new stimulus, to test whether the memory carries across contexts and whether it is specific to AP-1 target loci or global.

rewrites.title: Persistence regression with lineage tracing and mediation analysis
rewrites.description: Expose cells to a transient stimulus, withdraw it, and track barcoded clones over many divisions with longitudinal scATAC/scRNA, regressing later response amplitude on past exposure dose. Then run mediation analysis to ask how much of the persistence coefficient is carried by retained AP-1 motif accessibility/FOS-JUN occupancy versus alternative carriers such as DNA methylation, H3K4me1, BAF retention, or residual protein.

rewrites.title: Longitudinal chromatin profiling of patient biopsies across a stimulus cycle
rewrites.description: Collect paired biopsies or blood samples from the same patients at baseline, peak activation, and after resolution, then run ATAC-seq and FOS/JUN CUT&RUN. If memory exists, AP-1 motif accessibility and JUN/FOS occupancy should stay elevated at loci induced during the flare even after clinical and transcriptional markers return to baseline, and this persistence should be specific to AP-1 motifs compared with matched control motifs such as CEBP or RUNX.

rewrites.title: Mitotic bookmarking and inheritance fidelity across the cell cycle
rewrites.description: Combine live imaging of tagged AP-1 with cell-cycle sensors and post-mitotic chromatin profiling of daughter pairs to ask whether AP-1 sites are re-established after mitosis, and whether the two daughters inherit matched or divergent states. Measuring inheritance fidelity per division expresses memory as a per-generation transmission probability.

rewrites.title: Pulse-washout-rechallenge chromatin time course
rewrites.description: Expose cells to a brief, defined stimulus pulse (e.g., TNF, serum, or a MEK inhibitor), wash it out, and then profile ATAC-seq plus CUT&RUN for Fos/Jun family members at a dense series of timepoints spanning hours to weeks after washout. Memory is supported if a subset of AP-1-bound accessible regions remains open long after AP-1 protein levels and upstream signaling have returned to baseline, and if rechallenge produces a faster or larger response specifically at those retained sites.

rewrites.title: Timed degron depletion to separate establishment from maintenance
rewrites.description: Prime cells with a transient stimulus, then acutely degrade FOS/JUN (dTAG/AID) at different times after washout, before restimulation. If memory (faster or stronger transcription, retained accessibility) is lost upon late depletion, AP-1 is needed to maintain it, not only to establish it.

rewrites.title: Cell fusion or nuclear transfer to test chromatin-based versus AP-1 level-based memory
rewrites.description: Fuse primed cells with naive cells (heterokaryons, with species-polymorphic SNPs to assign alleles) or transfer primed nuclei into naive cytoplasm, then ask whether primed enhancers stay open in cis while naive-derived ones remain closed. Cis-restricted persistence argues for chromatin-based memory, while trans-spreading implicates diffusible factors such as AP-1 levels or feed-forward loops.

rewrites.title: Timed degron cohorts to separate maintenance from readout
rewrites.description: Use dTAG/auxin-degron FOS, JUN, and FRA-1 lines with a pulse stimulus, then degrade AP-1 in different cohorts during distinct windows (during the pulse, during the stimulus-free interval, or only at re-challenge), with each dish measured exactly once at a fixed endpoint. If degradation only during the stimulus-free interval erases enhanced recall, AP-1 protein is actively maintaining the memory, not merely reading it out.

rewrites.title: Time-resolved AP-1 occupancy versus histone marks with timed degradation
rewrites.description: After a stimulus, use SNAP/Halo-tagged FOS pulse-chase and sequential ChIP-seq at multiple time points to build a time-resolved record of AP-1 occupancy alongside histone marks such as H3K27ac and H3K4me1 at each enhancer. If memory exists, enhancers that keep their marks after AP-1 dissociates should be the ones that stay accessible, and acutely degrading AP-1 at a chosen time point should then test whether the marks are necessary to hold that state.
